card.identity: A jail guard on Schroeder's cell block who quietly believes the case against him is wrong. Risked his pension to help; uneasy, wary, and quick to pull back whenever the plan turns dangerous.
invariants: Is a jail guard
Sympathizes with Schroeder

sample.reason: Invents the guard name, pension risk and cautious temperament.

value.description: Nijō Seika’s headquarters in Kyoto: a narrow 1920s wooden building attached to a modern office block and the old confectionery factory. The archive smells of sugar, camphor and old paper. The centennial reception is being prepared downstairs.

sample.reason: Invents Kyoto, building history, sensory detail and centennial reception.

card.identity: An unaging man who has wandered for centuries without learning why his body never changes. Wary, watchful and used to moving on, he keeps a battered journal of every clue he has gathered and wakes bound and hooded in a stranger's wagon.
invariants: His body does not age.
He is searching for the cause and meaning of his condition.
He does not trust strangers quickly.

sample.reason: Adds centuries of wandering, journal, temperament and distrust.

card.identity: Nijō Ayame, 56, Takamasa’s younger sister and the company’s master confectioner. Beloved by employees for remembering names and birthdays. Unmarried, she lives with her mother. Twelve years ago she found the 1998 file and began anonymous quarterly payments to the victim’s daughter through a dormant supplier account.
invariants: She is left-handed.
She never intended to steal from the company.
She wants the 1998 cover-up exposed.

sample.reason: Invents Ayame and her age, family, payments and motive.

value.description: A narrow junction where the medieval escape passage meets the old service gallery, the only approach wide enough for the invaders' war machines. Hollis's autocannon emplacement commands it behind stacked rails and salvaged plate.

sample.reason: Adds junction geometry, machines, fortification and named gunner.

value.description: Four long white barns and a pole shed north of town, holding roughly two thousand head through winter. Ammonia haze, wet concrete, silage dust, the roar of blowers at dawn. Over a winter the manure packs into a thick layer that the pigs are loosed onto in spring. The north barn has its own gate, its own lock, and its own set of rules.

sample.reason: Adds named barns, count, sensory details and locked north barn.

value.description: Third person limited past tense, anchored to Danny, with a wry comic register that turns tender without breaking character. Chapters are scene-based and roughly equal in length; one chapter carries the childhood prank flashback.

sample.reason: Chooses viewpoint, tense, chapter balance and narrative register.

card.identity: Consume's friend, a girl named Carry, fated to Carry Water. Practical, loud, loyal. She works the kiln's water line and is the only person in Sallow who treats Consume's fate as a joke rather than a verdict.

sample.reason: Invents Carry, water-line role and relationship to Consume.

value.description: The Ashur tablets describe an imperial bureau that collected death-phrases, matched citizens to their mates and used the pairs to execute anyone the throne wished dead. The tablets claim three empires fell when that index was lost or stolen. One column names a final phrase, still legible, said to end the last heir of the line.

sample.reason: Adds imperial bureau, index mechanics, named tablets and heir.

value.description: Close third-person investigation in the manner of Keigo Higashino: evidence first, interviews that revise the reader’s understanding, and twists that arise from human loyalty rather than coincidence.

sample.reason: Adds close-third viewpoint and specific investigative method.

value.description: A wide, half-dead landscape of burnt orchards, salt-cracked roads, flooded foundations and abandoned towers, crossed by the riders' wagon route.

sample.reason: Adds burnt orchards, salt roads, towers and route details.

card.identity: The village Reader, old and half-blind, named Read and fated to Read Names. Keeper of the Naming Bell and the Name Book. She is bound to the rite and proud of it, but the Book has taught her how often a reading has been stretched, and she is tired of being certain.

sample.reason: Invents Reader, rite, bell, book and internal conflict.

card.identity: Marius Voss, 52, owns clubs and laundries in the Lumen District and works as a local fixer and violent enforcer. He owns Eddie's debt and controls the public side of the drug network. He keeps Delia close as a symbol of his success, believing he made her and controls her, while she built the business beneath him. He ordered Eddie to keep Delia away during a dockside deal. He wants to maintain control and punish betrayal.
invariants: Believes he owns everyone around him.
Punishes betrayal with public violence.
Does not know Delia built the network.

sample.reason: Invents Marius, age, businesses, debts and power structure.

card.identity: Sixty-one, owner of the largest barn complex in the county, a pillar of the co-op board and the church building fund. Genial in public, exacting in the barn aisle. Believes he built the town's prosperity and that frugality is a virtue others are too soft to practice. Pays well, remembers favors, and treats loyalty as a debt owed rather than a gift given.
invariants: Never admits the scheme is dishonest, only that it is efficient
Uses generosity as leverage
Protects the family name above all

sample.reason: Invents Harlan, age, public roles, temperament and leverage.

authorQuote.quote: a conspiracy led by Commissioner Gaider

card.identity: The commissioner who leads the conspiracy Schroeder uncovers.

sample.reason: All semantic content is the author-provided commissioner leading a conspiracy; no invented trait.

value.description: The phoenix-eagle warns that greed will undo the wisher's heart's desire. This is not a distant threat but a condition of the gift: any attempt to use the feather for gain, revenge or ownership destroys the very thing the wisher hoped to keep.

sample.reason: Adds precise punitive wish mechanics and destroys-what-is-kept consequence.

value.description: A flooded transit station and its adjoining medieval escape tunnels beneath the ruined city, converted into humanity's last refuge: sleeping tiers, hydroponic racks, a generator gallery, a hospital alcove, and a single defended shaft up to the dead surface.

sample.reason: Adds transit station, flooding, generators, hospital and shaft.

value.description: A climate-controlled depository beneath a decommissioned customs warehouse outside Trieste. Rows of steel drawers hold stolen tablets, ledgers and the wrists of the dead, cataloged by phrase. The Curator calls it a library. Everyone else calls it a graveyard.

sample.reason: Invents Vault, location, catalogue and Curator.

card.identity: Peter Corrigan is Dana's husband, a calm software engineer who handles paperwork and asks practical questions about the property. He trusts experts and inspectors, which makes Mara's private knowledge of the garden especially dangerous.

sample.reason: Invents Peter Corrigan, occupation and spouse relationship.

value.stance: Ayame has sent anonymous quarterly restitution to Hina for twelve years, without the family’s knowledge.

sample.reason: Invents Ayame/Hina, payment history and secrecy.

value.description: The central tension: can two people who loved each other stay close without turning the friendship into a postponed romance, a consolation prize, or a threat to their new partners?

sample.reason: Adds postponed romance, consolation prize and threat-to-partners framing.

value.description: Harlan gave Caleb work when no one else would, paid for the furnace repair the winter June was sick, and expects that debt repaid in silence. Caleb's moral code and his family's need pull in opposite directions: speaking up costs the wage, staying quiet costs something less visible but harder to carry.

sample.reason: Invents named characters, favors, furnace repair, debts and wage tradeoff.

card.identity: A game-design student whose capstone project is the reason she must take the department-showcase stage. Offstage she is articulate and obsessive about her craft; onstage her crippling stage fright turns every presentation into a physical ordeal—sweating palms, a hammering heart, thoughts that scatter. She has spent the term building a game and dodging the spotlight, and the presentation is the wall she cannot walk around.
invariants: Has crippling stage fright.
Is a game-design student presenting a capstone project.

sample.reason: Invents Mara, student identity, capstone, term and avoidance history.

value.description: Hope and despair in the refuge are separated only by small physical facts: a burning lamp, a counted round, a spoken name. Despair is never argued away, only postponed by an action or a duty.

sample.reason: Adds physical symbols and action/duty rule beyond supplied themes.

value.description: The glowing feather grants exactly one wish, and only a selfless one. A wish made to possess, punish or hoard turns the feather cold and ash-grey; greed undoes the wisher's heart's desire rather than fulfilling it. The wish's wording matters, but the heart behind it matters more.

sample.reason: Adds ash-grey feather, punitive mechanism and intent-versus-wording rule.

card.identity: Consume's father, named Keep, whose fate is read as Keep the Bees. A beekeeper with a ruined shoulder and a soft voice. He believes a name is a door and not a wall, and he has spent years quietly proving it to himself before he dares say it aloud.

sample.reason: Invents Keep, profession, shoulder injury and philosophy.

card.identity: A lean, clever jackal with a rust-red coat and a voice like a flute. He steals Balam not from malice alone but because his pups are starving in a flooded den. He is a trickster who trusts no one, yet he understands debt and is moved by unexpected mercy.

sample.reason: Adds jackal appearance, voice, starving pups and motivation.

card.identity: Theo is Claire's three-year-old son and Mara's grandson. He is curious, fast, and drawn to bright berries. During a weekend visit he gets into the porch bed and puts a belladonna berry in his mouth, triggering the story's near-tragic mishap. He survives after emergency treatment.

sample.reason: Invents Theo, family, age and exact mishap/recovery.

card.identity: Matsunaga Hina, 34, daughter of Kiyoko Matsunaga, who died in a 1998 factory accident. She runs a small bakery in Kyoto. She received years of anonymous restitution, then demanded answers. She possesses a maintenance report warning that the machine’s safety guard was removed.
invariants: She never asked for more than restitution.
She kept the maintenance report.

sample.reason: Invents Hina, accident, bakery, restitution and maintenance report.

card.identity: Mara Voss, 36, Elias's wife and a former restoration painter, now living in a care room with an illness doctors cannot name. Lucid in short windows, she remembers a childhood summer when she saw a door hanging in the air and touched it. She loves Elias enough to hide her pain from him and has never told him the full price of that first touch.
invariants: Mara touched the veil as a child and is threaded to it.
Mara chooses her own sacrifice; Elias never forces it.

sample.reason: Invents Mara Voss, illness, marriage, veil history and chosen sacrifice.

value.description: The dream forest: dense, wet, older than language. A purple-green glow pools in the moss and hangs under the canopy like low weather, so the whole wood seems lit from within. Trampled paths of light run between the trunks toward a single ancient tree whose roots hold a levitating crystal.

sample.reason: Adds Velawood name and substantial atmosphere beyond prompt.

card.identity: A mounted band of scavengers who live by stripping ruined towns. They speak a trade tongue Peter does not know, and they are divided over whether their captive should be sold to the Collector or sheltered from him.

sample.reason: Adds named group, scavenger economy, language and Collector conflict.

value.description: The Velawood pulls Iona out of her waking life; Dara and the sleep clinic pull her back toward it. Each night of the dream costs her a piece of the ordinary world, and she begins to suspect she is being spent on purpose.

sample.reason: Invents Iona, Dara, clinic and dream cost mechanism.

value.stance: Former partners of three years, now trying to be friends. Owen is afraid that honesty will cost him her entirely, so he practices it badly and then better.

sample.reason: Adds names, three-year duration, particular fear and emotional arc.

value.description: A diner built into a retired railcar at the edge of town. Cracked red vinyl booths, good coffee, a jukebox that skips. Nadia and Owen use it for their standing Saturday check-ins, and later for the double date.

sample.reason: Invents diner name, structure, furnishings and regular meetings.

authorQuote.quote: Detective Schroeder sits alone in his cell, determined to prove he didn’t kill his daughter.

card.identity: A detective held alone in a cell, determined to prove he did not kill his daughter.
invariants: Is a detective
Is confined in a cell
Believes he did not kill his daughter
Works to prove his innocence

sample.reason: Author supplies detective, confinement, daughter accusation and determination; belief is entailed by that determination.

card.identity: Mara Ellison, 63, a retired high-school chemistry teacher, has lived alone in the bungalow for twelve years. She is methodical, dryly funny, and quietly ashamed of how much of her life the garden has consumed. She is selling the house to move into a condo near her daughter Claire and grandson Theo, three. She knows the toxic plants by leaf, berry, and root, keeps a removal log, and has never told a buyer, neighbor, or city official the full truth about the garden. Her twelve years of pulling have become both penance and identity.
invariants: She has pulled invasive, poisonous plants from the garden for twelve years.
She is the homeowner selling the house.
She keeps a written log of plant removals.

sample.reason: Invents Mara, age, profession, family, removal log and sale motive.

value.description: The Civic Directorate wants the erasure to remain permanent so its ordered peace survives. The Rememberers, a rival resistance faction, want to seize the archive and restore all memories at any cost. Both factions vie for control of the city, and both want Mara as their key.

sample.reason: Adds faction names, specific goals, archive strategy and named key person.

card.identity: A luminous bird of flame and gold, vast enough to fill the shrine's darkness with daylight. It speaks in a voice of embers and rain. It offers a single glowing feather that grants one selfless wish, and it warns plainly that greed will undo the wisher's heart's desire.

sample.reason: Adds shrine-filling size and voice of embers/rain to supplied bird.

card.identity: Consume's mother, named Mend, whose fate is read as Mend What Breaks. A seamstress and mender of nets, patient and exact. She carries the weight of the village's judgment and answers it with work and silence, but she will not let her daughter be made into a stranger.

sample.reason: Invents Mend, profession, name interpretation and temperament.

card.identity: Vera's former student and sometime field partner, now a well-paid consultant to museums and private collectors. Charming, anxious, in debt. He sold the location of the Ashur dig to the Curator's people and tells himself he did it to keep Vera from being killed.

sample.reason: Invents Aldo, debt, student relationship and betrayal.

card.identity: A lifelong atheist and retired structural engineer, 71 at death. Precise, ironic, allergic to comfort language. Grew up in a loud Catholic household in a river town and spent his life proving he needed no one's heaven. His skepticism is honest rather than cruel, but it has cost him. He keeps a mental ledger of every choice he considers a failure.
invariants: Never claims religious belief before death
Thinks in measurements, tolerances and load paths
Deflects sincerity with dry precision

sample.reason: Invents Elias, profession, age, childhood, temperament and thought patterns.

value.description: Nijō Seika needs a bank loan for its centennial expansion. The bank auditor has flagged ¥21.6 million in unexplained adjustments, and the family wants the matter resolved quietly before the review.

sample.reason: Invents bank loan, centennial expansion, amount and quiet audit goal.

card.identity: Mara's game-development tutor and mentor, a working indie developer who teaches part-time. Calm, practical, allergic to platitudes; he gives Mara concrete tactics for public speaking rather than reassurance. His office is cluttered with dev kits and sticky notes. He believes fear is a level to be playtested, not a wall to be avoided, and his advice becomes Mara's toolkit onstage.

sample.reason: Invents Quinn, occupation details, office and specific teaching approach.

card.identity: Nijō Ren, 31, Takamasa’s son and heir, recently returned to the family firm. Polished and earnest, but strained. He discovered Ayame’s secret payments and the 1998 file, then diverted additional money through the same ghost account to keep the victim’s daughter from going public.
invariants: He is not the source of the audit leak.
He used Ayame’s archive card without her knowledge.

sample.reason: Invents Ren, age, role, account diversion and stolen archive access.

card.identity: Kuroda Shōichi, 61, chief financial officer with thirty-five years at Nijō Seika. Passed over for president years ago. He discovered the ghost-account anomalies and leaked them to the bank auditor, hoping to force a sale to a rival confectioner that has promised him a seat on its board.

sample.reason: Invents Kuroda, age, tenure, leak and board-seat motive.

value.description: In the white room, a truthful answer summons the past as lived experience rather than as story: Elias feels the room around him, hears voices, smells the air. He cannot skip ahead or edit what he sees; he can only choose what to admit.

sample.reason: Adds truthful-answer summons and prohibition on editing memories.

value.description: Danny's reflex to mock what he does not understand keeps colliding with Nora's refusal to explain herself on demand. Each misunderstanding forces him to choose between being right and being close.

sample.reason: Adds named siblings, refusal-to-explain dynamic and closeness-versus-rightness arc.

value.description: Close third person, past tense, anchored almost entirely in Vera's senses and inferences; brief shifts only when the plot requires Ines's private knowledge to be withheld. Thriller pacing with short chapters, concrete physical detail and no omniscient summary of the world's history.

sample.reason: Chooses perspective, tense, focalization, chapter pacing and history delivery.

value.description: Close third person, mostly on Consume, with a few chapters following her parents so the weight of expectation and the village's fear are felt from inside. Past tense, plain and concrete prose.

sample.reason: Chooses viewpoint shifts, tense and prose style.
